summary: member-of:room_members(room_id, member_id) makes the framework emit the EXISTS guard you'd otherwise hand-write into every flow: a row of the protected table is in scope when EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM room_members WHERE room_members.room_id = <table>.<join> AND room_members.member_id = <you>). Applied on EVERY surface - list, single-row read, update, delete, batch, versioning, ?include=, workflow transitions, locks.
join_semantics: <join_col> joins the membership table to the protected table: when the protected table HAS a column of that name (messages.room_id), rows match on it; when it doesn't, the protected table must BE the parent and rows match on its id (rooms.id = room_members.room_id). One declaration covers both the parent and its children.

A table without the join column counts as the parent only when the membership join column points at it: a foreign key / schema.prisma relation from <mt>.<join_col> to it; or, for the groups membership table and its key, groups.bootstrap.org_table; or, with no foreign key declared on that column, the conventional name (<singular>_id or <table>_id: room_id → rooms, company_id → companies). Anything else is a misdeclared child (a renamed or missing join column): the runtime refuses every non-admin request on that table, creates included (404, the unmatched-route body); the fix is named by the write gate / benmore check, which refuse the file.

Explicit parent: `member-of:<mt>(<join_col>=id, <user_col>)` declares that this table is the parent, whatever its name or columns - use it for a parent the rules above cannot recognize (e.g. spaces with space_members.area_id and no relation).
<user_col> identifies the member: compared against the session's numeric user id, or the session email when the column name contains 'email'.
example_app_yaml:
access:
  rooms:
    read: member-of:room_members(room_id, member_id)
    write: everyone        # anyone may create a room
  room_members:
    all: member-of:room_members(room_id, member_id)   # members see the roster
  messages:
    all: member-of:room_members(room_id, member_id)
  tasks:
    all: member-of:room_members(room_id, member_id)
behavior_notes: Founder auto-join: creating a row in a parent table (join targets its id) auto-inserts the creator's membership row (idempotent; group key + user_id columns on the membership table are auto-populated when present). Without it the creator couldn't read back the room they just made. If the membership table has other NOT NULL columns without defaults the auto-join fails LOUDLY: X-Member-Of-AutoJoin response header + a log line - insert the membership row yourself in that case.

Child-table create/update guard: POSTing a message requires membership in the room_id it points at (404 on a non-member parent so existence doesn't leak: the JSON {"error":"Not found"} a read of a missing row gets, the same for a missing, non-member or other-tenant parent); PATCHing the join column re-checks membership in the NEW parent.

A child table whose create is governed by another mode (`write: role:clinician` on visit_notes, while patients is read through member-of) is still tied to parents the caller can read: when the child's column is a declared relation to the parent, a create or re-pointing update that names a parent the caller cannot read answers 422 `<column> references a record that does not exist or is not accessible`, the same for a missing parent (api({at:'scoping'}) foreign_keys). 'A clinician writes notes only for patients they are assigned to' therefore needs no before_insert hook.

Tenant-safe: when the protected table also carries the groups: key, the tenant clause is AND'd - membership widens visibility within a tenant, never across. A caller with no tenant (removed from their company, or never in one) gains nothing there from membership rows: only an explicit share authorizes a row, and creates or re-points through membership answer 404. The one read they keep is on the groups: membership table itself, of the rows that name them (scoping.missing_group).

Roster rule (the membership table scoped by itself, `room_members: member-of:room_members(room_id, member_id)`): a member sees and, under `all:`, edits only the membership rows of rooms they belong to.
member-of REPLACES owner scoping on the governed op (members see each other's rows - that's the point). Record-level ACL grants (permissions API) still OR in.
Admins (not stepped into a tenant) bypass, like every mode. Malformed declarations fail closed - a typo 404s the endpoint instead of widening it; the write-time validator catches the syntax.

Real-time: WS/SSE mutation events for member-of tables carry only {table, action} - clients re-fetch through the gated API, so no row data leaks to non-members. To gate the WS ROOM itself (who may join/broadcast), pair with ws_rooms: - see api({at:'websocket'}).

A rule that names a membership table or column the app does not have is accepted and loads, and every request it gates fails for everyone but admins (a server error, never rows). `benmore check` and the answer to a write of app.yaml warn about it once per table and rule, naming the operations it is written for and the app's tables or the membership table's columns. A membership table or view that one of the app's migrations/ files creates counts as present, and its columns are not judged from the sources.
